newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end mostly up on higher cash quotes.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end mostly up on higher cash quotes.

text.p: The continued strong tone to cash lumber supported most CME lumber futures contracts at the close, traders said.
Lumber closed off $1.20 per thousand board feet to up $3.40 with only May off at $385.50 and July up $1.00 at $380.20 per tbf.

Cash prices continued to rise, but nearby futures ran into chart selling under $392 per cwt. Resistance also stemmed from somewhat slower 2X4 sales. Wide widths have been the most active and not futures type 2X4's, traders said.
Rising interest rates may also have limited upside potential, they said.

Random Lengths early Friday quoted cash spruce at $390 per tbf, up $7 from midweek and $18 above last Friday. Trading increased and prices rose when it became clear there was no "wall of wood" waiting to cross the border from Canada at the start of the new quota year on April 1, traders said.
